audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Rumble levels 2 and 3 while the prose in the same entry says those levels are "genuinely his window" for Maokai, and Rumble only wins 46.41% over 487 games.
audit.why: Twisted Advance (W) unlocks at level 2 on a 14s cooldown at rank 1; by 3 he adds Sapling Toss (E, 18s). Rumble has no dash and no way to interrupt an untargetable dash, so those two levels belong to Maokai.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 and 3 flipped to Maokai in both layers (content win[1..2], full phases[1..2].side) with ratings dropped to 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named the level-2 spike but omitted the concrete cooldown that defines the window, and the level-3 spike (Sapling Toss) was absent from the phase text.
audit.why: Twisted Advance 14/13/12/11/10s and Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14s are the numbers that tell the player how long the safe window actually is. Nature's Grasp (130/110/90) and The Equalizer (130/105/80) are near-identical, so neither side gets a lasting ult-cooldown edge.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and phases[1..2].why now carry the 14s and 18s numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were never stated: (a) Twisted Advance makes Maokai untargetable for the whole dash, so Electro Harpoon cannot stop or trade into it; (b) Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist, and two of them make Flamespitter and The Equalizer hit a tank far harder; (c) Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced every time an enemy spell strikes Maokai, so Flamespitter's repeated ticks actively accelerate his sustain.
audit.why: All three come straight from Riot's own ability descriptions. (c) is the reason chip-poking a Maokai does less than it looks and why Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades — flagged in _missing-interactions as needs-antiheal.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[1], whys[3], spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], wants.foe[2], dosFull[2].d and phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The punishable-cooldown advice was generic ("track it") with no duration.
audit.why: Twisted Advance at 14s rank 1 falling to 10s rank 5 is the single window in the lane; the numbers make the advice actionable.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] was titled "Fight in saplings" but its detail text was unrelated boilerplate about burning a cooldown for tiny value; dosFull[2] was titled "Flame %HP-poke from range" with detail text about Twisted Advance instead.
audit.why: Title and body contradicted each other, so neither entry taught anything.
audit.corrected: Both detail strings rewritten to match their titles with real numbers (Sapling Toss 18s, brush bonus; Electro Harpoon MR shred).

edits.before: The moment Maokai hits level 2 he has Twisted Advance: one root-dash forces him into your Flamespitter range AND locks you in place, flipping the early trade pattern completely.
edits.after: Level 2 brings Twisted Advance, and he is untargetable through the dash — no Electro Harpoon stops it, and the root pins you inside Bramble Smash. It is down 14s at rank 1.

edits.before: Double-E slow him as he tries to walk back after Twisted Advance expires so he eats the full Danger Zone Q duration
edits.after: Land both Electro Harpoons — each shreds his Magic Resist, so the slow that holds him also makes Flamespitter hit harder

edits.before: Let his passive Sap Magic sustain chip Flamespitter damage back over time while he waits for Twisted Advance cooldowns
edits.after: Heal your Flamespitter chip off with Sap Magic — every Q tick striking him cuts that heal's cooldown further

edits.before: Twisted Advance hits at level 2: his lock-on root-dash plants you in place mid-trade and he can dump his full auto-enhanced kit on a rooted Rumble who cannot reposition his W shield.
edits.after: Twisted Advance hits at level 2 and he is untargetable through the dash — no harpoon interrupts it. Rooted, you eat Bramble Smash, whose knockback shoves you out of your own Flamespitter cone.

edits.before: With Twisted Advance on cooldown you own a clean window: Danger Zone Q across his body, Scrap Shield to tank his autos, double Electro-Harpoon to stop him walking back, reset before Heat caps.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is down 14s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5 — that is your window: Danger Zone Q across his body, Scrap Shield the autos, both Electro Harpoons to shred his MR and pin him, reset before Heat caps.

edits.before: Heat management is the kit: ride 50-100, never overheat by accident. Only take the trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is online and he is untargetable mid-dash — no harpoon stops it. Give the wave rather than contesting a root.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Maokai must walk into your range.
edits.after: Sapling Toss adds an 18s zone that hits harder in brush. Farm at max Flamespitter range until his level-4 lull.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Sapling Toss is 18s and stronger in brush — step off the plant.

edits.before: Maokai wastes Twisted Advance (Root) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Both Electro Harpoons shred his Magic Resist, so every later tick hurts more.

notes: Packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES — "Twisted Advance" is the correct name of Maokai W in both flagged spots; no rename made. Two derived-flag misfires in the kit files, both contradicted by Riot's own descriptions and therefore NOT used: rumble.json flags Scrap Shield (W) with "knockup" and "terrain" (it is only a shield plus a move-speed burst), and flags The Equalizer (R) as "projectile" (it is a ground-targeted line, not a blockable missile). Maokai Bramble Smash (Q) carries a "grounding" flag; Rumble has no dash or blink, so grounding was deliberately left out under the relevance rule. Level 1 left as "Skill" in both layers rather than flipped — the prose supports Rumble there, but with a 46.41% win rate over 487 games I only corrected the two stages the entry's own text already contradicted.
